surface: lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint write guard (internal/tds isEndpointWrite) and Class B strict mode (internal/tsql CheckStrict, -tsql-strict)

unsupported.text: `BULK LOAD`, though `bcp` is supported as a preview feature.
unsupported.reason: Guard: BULK is a denied keyword in isEndpointWrite. Strict mode has no BULK check, so only the lakehouse endpoint refuses it; a Warehouse forwards it either way.

Strict mode refuses it. The endpoint guard allow-lists USER beside ROLE, so with strict mode off it is forwarded; whether that was deliberate is not recorded. The emulator provisions each caller's database user itself (internal/tds/principal.go).

unsupported.text: `FOR JSON` must be the last operator in the query, so you can't use it inside subqueries.
probes: SELECT (SELECT a FROM dbo.t FOR JSON PATH) AS j
unsupported.reason: Neither refuses it. Strict mode says why: FOR JSON is legal as the last operator, so telling a subquery's from it needs a real parse, not a lexer (internal/tsql/strict.go). A candidate for the sqlglot-go tree.

probes: CREATE STATISTICS s ON dbo.t (a, b)
unsupported.reason: Refused by the guard (CREATE outside its allow-list) and by strict mode.

probes: CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW dbo.mv AS SELECT 1 AS x
CREATE UNIQUE CLUSTERED INDEX ix ON dbo.v (a)
unsupported.reason: Guard: neither MATERIALIZED VIEW nor CREATE INDEX is in the allow-list, and SQL Server's spelling of a materialized view is an indexed view, i.e. a view plus a clustered index. Strict mode does not enforce it: that needs CREATE INDEX correlated with its view across statements (internal/tsql/strict.go).

probes: SELECT * FROM PREDICT(MODEL = dbo.m, DATA = dbo.t) AS p
unsupported.reason: Strict mode refuses it. With it off the guard forwards it, as a read, and SQL Server would run it.

unsupported.text: Queries targeting system and user tables
unsupported.reason: The sentence names no statement, so there is nothing to probe. Left unclassified rather than guessed; strict mode notes it as a system-table question a lexer cannot see.

probes: WITH r AS (SELECT 1 AS n UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM r WHERE n < 3) SELECT * FROM r
unsupported.reason: Strict mode refuses it. With it off the guard forwards it, as a read, and SQL Server accepts recursive CTEs.

unsupported.text: Schema and table names can't contain `/` or `\`
probes: CREATE VIEW dbo.[a/b] AS SELECT 1 AS x
CREATE VIEW dbo.[a\b] AS SELECT 1 AS x
unsupported.reason: Neither refuses it: VIEW is allow-listed and no check reads object names. Not in strict mode's list at all, and cheap to add: a quoted identifier is one lexer token.

probes: SELECT a FROM dbo.t FOR XML PATH
unsupported.reason: Strict mode refuses it. With it off the guard forwards it, as a read, and SQL Server accepts FOR XML.
Strict mode refuses it. With it off SET is not a write, so the guard forwards it.

probes: SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED
unsupported.reason: Strict mode refuses it. With it off SET is not a write, so the guard forwards it.
Refused by strict mode, and by the guard only because EXEC is refused wholesale on the endpoint, not because of this procedure.
Refused by the guard (CREATE outside its allow-list) and by strict mode.

probes: CREATE TRIGGER tr ON dbo.t AFTER INSERT AS SELECT 1
unsupported.reason: Refused by the guard (CREATE outside its allow-list) and by strict mode.

unsupported.text: Vector data type and search functions
probes: CREATE VIEW dbo.v AS SELECT CAST(NULL AS vector(3)) AS e
unsupported.reason: Neither refuses it. Strict mode's own reasoning stands: the sidecar is SQL Server 2022, which has no vector type, so the engine refuses it anyway. That is a property of the engine's version, not of this emulator: a newer sidecar would accept it.
